questions.stem: For the equilibrium 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), what happens when the pressure is increased?

options.text: The equilibrium shifts to the left (3 moles of gas)
The equilibrium shifts to the right (2 moles of gas)
There is no effect because the moles are equal on both sides
The equilibrium shifts to the left because SO₃ is unstable

questions.explanation: There are 3 moles of gas on the left (2 SO₂ + 1 O₂) and 2 moles on the right (2 SO₃). Increasing pressure causes the system to oppose by reducing pressure, shifting towards the side with fewer gas moles. The equilibrium shifts to the right, producing more SO₃.

questions.stem: In the equilibrium N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g) where N₂O₄ is colourless and NO₂ is brown, the forward reaction is endothermic. What colour change would you see if the temperature is decreased?

options.text: The mixture becomes lighter/paler as more colourless N₂O₄ forms

questions.explanation: Decreasing temperature causes the system to oppose by favouring the exothermic direction, which is the reverse reaction (forming N₂O₄). More colourless N₂O₄ is produced and less brown NO₂ remains, so the mixture becomes lighter or paler.
